name: Asymmetric Huber (pinball)
tagline: Asymmetric Huber loss: smooth-L1 (quadratic for small errors, linear for large) with pinball weights {tau, 1-tau} for over/under-estimation.

key_hyperparams.name: tau (quantile)
key_hyperparams.role: asymmetry: target high quantile of Q

diff_from_baseline: Combines Huber loss (Huber 1964) with quantile/pinball weighting (Koenker & Bassett 1978). Quadratic regime keeps gradients well-behaved while linear tails control the influence of outlier Q-targets, retaining IQL's high-quantile target.

name: Quantile (pinball L1)
tagline: Asymmetric L1 (pinball) loss: weighted absolute error with {1-tau, tau} weights for over/under-estimation; estimates the conditional tau-quantile of Q(s,a).
diff_from_baseline: Koenker & Bassett 1978 (pinball loss); used in distributional RL e.g. QR-DQN (Dabney et al., AAAI 2018). Replaces IQL's expectile (asymmetric L2) with the standard quantile loss — same asymmetry but L1 magnitudes for outlier robustness.

name: Expectile (IQL default)
tagline: Default IQL value loss: asymmetric L2 (expectile regression) that pushes V(s) toward a high expectile (tau=0.9) of Q(s,a) without explicit max over actions.
diff_from_baseline: Kostrikov et al., "Offline Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Q-Learning" (ICLR 2022). The reference IQL value loss: expectile regression weights squared TD errors asymmetrically so V approaches a high expectile of the in-distribution Q. Reference comparator for the task.
